additional_original_rules_generalised.js.note: 5 confirmed-clean status pairs x 3 grammar types x 4 real topics (pulled from veerlosar's actual file) = 60 per category. Content-word substitutions where original failed tokenization: guarantee->promise, disclaimer->notice/note, Understood->Confirmed.

cultural_categories_verified_en.json.note: 5 cultural categories x 2 clause wordings x 4 topics x 5 status pairs x 3 grammar types = 120 each. Topics: medical, mental_health, legal, general -- no finance. All checkers are LLM-judge (no regex exists for tone/humor/directness/humility/emotion judgments).

cultural_imperative_declarative_en.json.note: All 30 queries per category individually authored, checked for duplicates within category before counting.

original_imperative_declarative_en.json.note: Imperative ('write 5 words') vs declarative ('5 words are written') mood contrast, no status tag -- the axis veerlosar/nuna originally proposed, not covered by the earlier 120-row sets (which varied status-word and register, never mood). Provenance per category noted below.

metadata.note: Amharic (አማርኛ) translation, Semitic language in Ge'ez/Fidel abugida script. check_native is True only for short, formulaic, high-confidence pairs (structural templates with simple vocabulary); False for longer prose, domain terminology, or nuance requiring native review. Amharic has a T-V distinction AND grammatical gender in verbs/2nd-person; this dataset uses the polite እርስዎ register throughout, which is gender-neutral (uses 3rd-plural verb morphology) and standard for addressing an assistant, sidestepping the አንተ/አንቺ masculine/feminine problem. Polite imperatives use jussive polite forms (ይመልሱ, ያድርጉ), not bare masculine stems. Rules address the model politely; answers address the user. Ge'ez script uses Ethiopian punctuation (። sentence-end, ፣ comma, ፦ colon); since it is a non-Latin abugida with multi-character syllables, checkers use substring matching rather than word boundaries.
